title: The Neighbour - ricercar a 4 on John Williams's Theme from Jurassic Park - symphony orchestra
comment: Final symphonic scoring of score/music-voices.ly (66 bars) with design/final-lab/plan.json. Strings are the backbone: every subject, answer and inversion entry starts in a string section (soprano vn1, alto vn2, tenor va, bass vc), and CS2 (the motor) always stays in the strings. Colour changes happen at phrase joins, Webern-fashion: where a voice turns from its subject into CS1 (the lament), the lament goes to a reed and walks down the woodwind family as it moves down the voices (soprano oboe 5:4, alto clarinet 9:4, bass bassoons 13:4; later bassoons 20:4, clarinet 35:4, bassoons 41:4, the tenor's lament lead-in 46 on the clarinet), and the line returns to its strings at the next join. The episode's sequence (18-20) is the flute's; the false dawn (20-26) glows with a clarinet on the tenor's D-flat major subject and an oboe on the soprano's G-flat major subject, both at the unison. Climax I (26:3-29) builds the E diminished seventh head by head in brass: bass head 26:3 bass trombone, tuba, timpani roll, basses 8vb, bassoons; tenor head 27:1 trombone, horns 3-4, clarinet; alto head 27:3 horns 1-2, oboe; soprano head 28:1 trumpet, flute 8va. The arioso dolente (30-33) is a woodwind choir (oboe S2, clarinets, bassoon) with a solo horn on the dominant F (32:3-34:1); at the German-sixth pivot (34:1) the same harmony passes to the strings, which carry the fuga inversa. Horns hold the pedal points: the dominant F under the augmented inversion (46:1-50:3, where the tenor's lament lead-in is the clarinet's and the alto's S2 the oboe's, as in the arioso) and the tonic B-flat of the coda (63-66). Climax II (50:3-53:4) is the second tutti: trumpets on the diminution heads (soprano, then alto at 52:1), horns and trombone on the tenor's S1, bass trombone, tuba, bassoons, basses 8vb on the augmented inversion, timpani (C3 an octave up where the bass goes below the drums, the low F on the V fermata). The hinge (54) is strings alone. Apotheosis: the whole tune in B-flat major on four horns (55-62) over the strings' triple counterpoint, with the bassoons doubling the lament in the bass; at 59 (the tune's second half, peak f at 60:4) the violins, flute 8va and trumpet join the horns and the low brass double the answer in the bass, over a timpani roll on F; at 63 the violins take the tune's d'' alone, the timpani toll the tonic pedal once a bar under the horns' held B-flat, and the subject's last B-flat A B-flat (65-66) is a solo horn. Octave doublings (flute 8va, basses 8vb) only in the three tuttis and on the coda's tonic pedal. Every part stays inside its compass (orch_common.PARTS): the alto's F3/F#3 (9:4-12:4) and its A3s are on the clarinet, the tenor's C3s on the viola, bass notes below E2 never on the tenor trombone, below D2 never on the timpani.
